answer: To deter Sybil attacks, agents anchor security at an ingress wharf where cross-cluster transactions cross an audited bridge. Multi-agent committees perform topological cut verifications on interaction graphs to detect clustered fake identities. When an adversarial gale of coordinated Sybils attempts a cut evasion, game-theoretic audits trigger stake slashing. This enforces a superlinear attacker cost scaling with the cut size.
